scope.scopeNotesMd: This report compares the core R4 `HealthcareService` StructureDefinition with the R6 ballot4 `HealthcareService` StructureDefinition and inspects directly relevant R6 datatypes and terminology used by changed local elements. It intentionally treats inherited `DomainResource`, `Resource`, `Element`, `Extension`, and primitive/datatype-wide changes as out of scope unless they are surfaced by a local `HealthcareService` element change. The R6 artifact is present at the expected canonical URL, so there is no rename/removal identity issue for the resource itself.
outOfScope: Inherited `DomainResource.language` binding changes shown in the snapshots are not reported as local `HealthcareService` findings; the local `HealthcareService.communication` binding change is reported separately because it is defined in the resource differential.

Inherited `DomainResource` constraints such as `dom-2` through `dom-6` and base `Element` constraints such as `ele-1` are out of scope except where a new local `HealthcareService` invariant was added.
SearchParameter changes, operations, profiles, implementation guide rules, and server capability impacts were not analyzed as local StructureDefinition breaking changes.

Datatype-wide behavior of `Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`, `markdown`, `CodeableConcept`, `Reference`, and base primitives is delegated to those artifact reports; this report only discusses their impact where `HealthcareService` locally adopted them.

narrativeReportMd:
# HealthcareService R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`HealthcareService` has material local breaking changes. Existing R4 instances that use direct `telecom`, `availableTime`, `notAvailable`, or `availabilityExceptions` elements will not validate as R6 without structural transformation, and `communication` coding is now constrained by a required BCP-47 language value set.

## Scope
The analysis is limited to local `HealthcareService` StructureDefinition changes plus directly relevant R6 dependency datatypes (`Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`) and terminology artifacts. Inherited base-resource and base-datatype changes are excluded from `findings[]`.

## Main migration themes
The largest migration theme is representation reshaping: direct R4 contact and availability elements moved into richer reusable datatypes. A second theme is stricter terminology for `HealthcareService.communication`. A third theme is R6-only service-discovery semantics (`offeredIn`, `referralRequired`, and richer eligibility values) that cannot be round-tripped to plain R4 without extensions or loss.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `HealthcareService:element-presence:telecom-contact:5d6f0b`, `HealthcareService:element-presence:availability:4c8a21`, and `HealthcareService:terminology:communication:9e31b7`. These affect validation, generated model shape, and migration transforms.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for availability migration and terminology validation. Availability has a plausible structural mapping but includes renamed children, a dropped direct exception-text element, a new `Availability.period`, and an `allDay` invariant. Language binding impact depends on whether real R4 data used BCP-47 language codings or local/service-specific codes.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most R6 changes look motivated by reusable, richer datatypes and clearer service directory semantics. Less disruptive alternatives existed for several changes, especially retaining deprecated aliases or cross-version extensions for old paths, but those alternatives would have preserved duplicate representations.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should assess the reusable `Availability` and `ExtendedContactDetail` datatypes, the inherited `DomainResource.language` binding change, and terminology expansion behavior for `all-languages`.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `HealthcareService` has high-impact local breaking changes: contact details moved from direct `telecom` to `contact`, availability moved into the `Availability` datatype, and `communication` now has a required language binding. The main uncertainty is terminology expansion/enforcement for language codes and real-world mapping policy for availability exceptions.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migrations should prioritize structural transforms before terminology cleanup. Direct R4 contact and availability properties must be rewritten into nested R6 datatypes. R4 communication codings should be audited for BCP-47 compliance. Down-conversion from R6 to R4 needs explicit policy for R6-only elements such as `offeredIn`, `referralRequired`, `eligibility.value[x]`, `eligibility.period`, and `Availability.period`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition changes because both assigned StructureDefinitions and relevant dependency definitions are present locally. Confidence is lower for terminology edge cases and design rationale because no official diff, ballot change notes, rendered narrative pages, or live terminology expansions were used.

findings.title: Direct `HealthcareService.telecom` was replaced by nested `HealthcareService.contact` using ExtendedContactDetail

oldState.summary: R4 represented service contact points directly as `HealthcareService.telecom` with type `ContactPoint` and cardinality `0..*`.

semanticText.short: Contacts related to the healthcare service
semanticText.definition: List of contacts related to this specific healthcare service.
semanticText.comment: If this is empty, then refer to the location's contacts.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances can place phone, fax, email, or URL contact points directly under `HealthcareService.telecom`.

newState.summary: R6 removed direct `telecom` and added `HealthcareService.contact` with type `ExtendedContactDetail` and cardinality `0..*`.

semanticText.short: Official contact details for the HealthcareService
semanticText.definition: The contact details of communication devices available relevant to the specific HealthcareService. This can include addresses, phone numbers, fax numbers, mobile numbers, email addresses and web sites.
semanticText.comment: The address/telecom use code 'home' are not to be used.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 contact information is carried in `contact`, whose datatype can hold `purpose`, `name`, `telecom`, `address`, `organization`, and `period`.

facts.note: The direct R4 element is absent from the R6 HealthcareService differential and snapshot.
The new local element carries richer contact detail records.
The ContactPoint data can be nested inside ExtendedContactDetail but is not wire-compatible.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `contact` definition explicitly describes the same communication channels as R4 `telecom`, and `ExtendedContactDetail` contains a `telecom: ContactPoint 0..*` child. The match is semantic rather than a simple rename because R6 adds purpose, names, addresses, organization, and period around the contact points.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A strict R6 parser or validator will reject R4 instances that still contain `HealthcareService.telecom` because that local element no longer exists. Generated R4 classes expose a repeated `ContactPoint`, while generated R6 classes expose repeated `ExtendedContactDetail`; code that reads or writes service contact points must change. Down-conversion can preserve plain telecom points but loses R6-only purpose, named contact, address, organization, and period unless extensions are used.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly migrated service contact details can affect scheduling, billing, booking, or patient-facing directory workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer official contact records for a healthcare service instead of only bare telecom points.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `telecom` in base R6 while adding richer `contact` records.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--modeling official service contacts with purpose, address, organization, name, and period--is reasonable and is supported by the move to `ExtendedContactDetail`. A less-breaking base design was possible, but it would leave two normative contact locations on the same resource and would require validators and clients to resolve conflicts. Given those material long-term interoperability costs, the break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative would have kept `HealthcareService.telecom` as deprecated `0..* ContactPoint` and added `HealthcareService.contact` for richer details, possibly with guidance to migrate simple telecom points into `contact.telecom`. That would preserve old R4-valid instances, but duplicate phone/email/url facts could diverge, and deprecated contact representations might remain indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances but creates duplicate same-resource contact representations that require reconciliation.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `telecom` as `ContactPoint 0..*`.
evidence.quote: List of contacts related to this specific healthcare service.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `contact` as `ExtendedContactDetail 0..*` and has no local `telecom` element.
evidence.quote: Official contact details for the HealthcareService

evidence.detail: `ExtendedContactDetail` includes nested `telecom` contact points plus additional contact context.

examples.examplesMd: The examples focus on the changed fields and omit unrelated optional content. A simple R4 `telecom` repetition can be wrapped as one R6 `contact` record, but richer R6 contact context has no native R4 target.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 replaces the direct `telecom` array with a richer `contact` array. This is a hard wire-format change for any existing R4 HealthcareService instances that publish service phone numbers, email addresses, or web URLs under `telecom`. The practical consequence is not just a field rename: the R6 datatype changes the application model from bare contact points to contact-detail records with optional purpose, responsible party, address, and effective period.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing `HealthcareService.telecom` can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6 because the element is no longer defined. Conversely, an R6 `contact` record cannot be represented in plain R4 without either flattening nested `contact.telecom` to `telecom` and discarding context, or carrying R6-only details in extensions. Strict parsers, JSON-schema-like validators, generated classes, and FHIRPath expressions that refer to `HealthcareService.telecom` are directly affected.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Transform R4 `telecom` repetitions into R6 `contact.telecom`. If the R4 data has no contact purpose, either create one `contact` with all telecom points or one `contact` per point based on local policy. For down-conversion, decide whether to flatten only `contact.telecom` or preserve `purpose`, `name`, `address`, `organization`, and `period` using extensions. Regression tests should include phone, email, URL, multiple contact points, and R6 contact records with non-telecom context.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer model is understandable, but removal of the old direct element was avoidable. Keeping `telecom` as deprecated would have allowed old instances to remain valid while encouraging new implementations to populate `contact`. The cost would be duplicated contact semantics and extra reconciliation rules.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm whether the official R6 migration guidance recommends one `ExtendedContactDetail` per R4 `ContactPoint` or grouping multiple R4 telecom entries into a single contact record.

findings.title: Availability details moved from three direct HealthcareService elements into the R6 Availability datatype

oldState.summary: R4 exposes availability as direct elements: `availableTime 0..*`, `notAvailable 0..*`, and `availabilityExceptions 0..1`.

semanticText.definition: R4 `availableTime` and `notAvailable` are local backbone elements; `availabilityExceptions` is a direct string for textual exceptions.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances carry schedule-like availability directly under the resource, including direct exception text and a required `notAvailable.description` when a `notAvailable` repetition is present.

newState.summary: R6 removes the direct availability elements and adds `HealthcareService.availability 0..1` of type `Availability`.

semanticText.definition: A collection of times that the healthcare service is available.
semanticText.comment: More detailed availability information may be provided in associated Schedule/Slot resources.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 nests availability information in `Availability`, with children such as `period`, `availableTime`, and `notAvailableTime`. The reusable datatype adds `av-1`, which disallows start/end times when `allDay` is true.

facts.note: R4 `notAvailable.description` is mandatory within each notAvailable repetition; R6 `Availability.notAvailableTime.description` is optional.

facts.newValue: av-1: allDay.exists().not() or (allDay implies availableStartTime.exists().not() and availableEndTime.exists().not())
facts.note: Constraint is defined on the R6 `Availability.availableTime` datatype element.
Textual exceptions may need mapping into `notAvailableTime.description` or extensions.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `availability` element has the same purpose and comments as the R4 availability group, and the R6 `Availability` datatype contains children corresponding to R4 `availableTime` and `notAvailable`, renamed/nested under the datatype. `availabilityExceptions` has no same-named R6 child and requires policy-based mapping.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Strict R6 validation rejects the old direct R4 availability fields. Runtime models and FHIRPath expressions must move from direct resource children to the nested `Availability` datatype. Down-conversion is lossy for `Availability.period`, R6 `notAvailableTime` entries without descriptions, and any representation of R4 `availabilityExceptions` that cannot be reduced to R4's single string field. The `av-1` invariant also makes a naive transform of some R4 `availableTime` records invalid when `allDay=true` is carried together with start or end times.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Availability drives service discovery and scheduling. Incorrect transforms can advertise wrong opening hours or hide closures.

justification.inferredGoal: Reuse a common `Availability` datatype across artifacts and consolidate availability semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated direct availability fields alongside the new `availability` datatype element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Reusing a common `Availability` datatype and consolidating availability semantics is a credible R6 goal. The less-breaking approach of retaining `availableTime`, `notAvailable`, and `availabilityExceptions` would preserve R4 data, but the tradeoffs are larger than for a simple alias: the same schedule could be represented in two shapes, exception text would need precedence rules, and conflicts could affect service-discovery or scheduling safety. The breaking consolidation is therefore probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base-compatible design could have kept the three R4 direct fields as deprecated aliases while adding `HealthcareService.availability`. That is a real alternative, not merely conversion tooling, but it would require cross-field consistency rules between direct and nested availability, and it risks indefinitely accumulating parallel schedule representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but duplicates scheduling semantics and adds validation ambiguity around exceptions and all-day rules.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `availableTime` as a local `BackboneElement 0..*`.
evidence.quote: A collection of times that the Service Site is available.

evidence.detail: R4 requires a description in each `notAvailable` repetition.
R4 has direct textual exception content.
R6 defines one optional `availability` element of type `Availability` and removes the old direct elements.
evidence.quote: Times the healthcare service is available (including exceptions)

evidence.detail: The R6 Availability datatype adds an all-day constraint not present on the R4 local backbone element.
evidence.quote: Cannot include start/end times when selecting all day availability.

examples.examplesMd: The old example demonstrates two independent validation effects: the direct R4 paths are not valid R6 paths, and a naive nested transform retaining `allDay=true` with a start time would violate R6 `av-1`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 consolidates service availability into a reusable `Availability` datatype. That changes the instance shape for all existing R4 data using `availableTime`, `notAvailable`, or `availabilityExceptions`. The change also has semantic differences: R6 can scope availability with `Availability.period`, makes not-available descriptions optional, and applies an all-day constraint to available times.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with the old direct fields can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6. A transformed R6 instance must satisfy the `Availability` datatype's constraints, including `av-1`; simply nesting old content can still fail if old data combined `allDay` with start/end times. Valid R6 availability cannot always be represented in R4 because R4 has no `Availability.period` and requires a different direct shape.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 `availableTime` to `availability.availableTime`, R4 `notAvailable` to `availability.notAvailableTime`, and decide how to map R4 `availabilityExceptions`—commonly to a `notAvailableTime.description` without `during`, or to an extension if the distinction must be preserved. Clean up any `allDay=true` records by removing start/end times or changing `allDay` to false based on business intent. Test direct-path rejection, nested-path acceptance, textual exceptions, not-available entries without periods, and all-day/time combinations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The consolidation is probably justified by reuse and consistency, but compatibility could have been improved by leaving the old direct elements as deprecated aliases or by publishing a normative cross-version extension for `availabilityExceptions`. The tradeoff would be duplicate schedule representations and extra validation complexity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Official migration guidance would be valuable for the exact handling of `availabilityExceptions` and for grouping multiple R4 availability repetitions into a single R6 `Availability` instance.

findings.title: `HealthcareService.communication` binding strengthened from preferred languages to required all-languages

oldState.summary: R4 binds `communication` to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/languages` with preferred strength.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 preferred binding encouraged common language codes but did not make non-language or local service-language codings invalid.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 systems could use the preferred `languages` value set for interoperability, but strict validation would not reject alternate codings solely because of this binding.

newState.summary: R6 binds `communication` to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4` with required strength.

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 value set composes all BCP-47 language tags (`urn:ietf:bcp:47`). A live expansion was not performed; the conformance impact is from required binding strength plus the expected system/domain.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes language coding a conformance requirement rather than only a recommendation.

facts.newValue: IETF language tag for a human language

facts.note: R6 keeps the smaller languages value set only as an additional starter binding.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct terminology validation tightening. R4 instances with `communication` codings outside the language value set could be valid because the binding was only preferred; R6 required binding can reject them. Runtime risk is high for validators, enum-generation, terminology services, and business rules that previously tolerated local codes such as interpreter-program flags in this element.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Language availability is operationally important for access and scheduling. Invalid or unmapped local codings can hide services from users who need language support.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure that the languages a service is offered in are represented as interoperable BCP-47 language tags.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use extensible/preferred binding or require a BCP-47 coding while allowing supplemental local codings.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of making `communication` carry interoperable human-language tags is reasonable because the element specifically describes languages a service is offered in. A less-breaking design could allow local supplemental codings or keep a weaker binding, but that either fails to guarantee BCP-47 language representation or only preserves cases that already include a valid BCP-47 coding. Because the alternatives only partially meet the interoperability goal, the required binding is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base design would avoid a fully required binding and instead use an extensible binding or an invariant requiring at least one `urn:ietf:bcp:47` coding while permitting additional local codings. This would reduce failures for mixed CodeableConcepts but would not preserve R4 instances that used only local non-language codes, and a purely preferred binding would not meet the goal of consistent language interoperability.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Less disruptive for legacy codings but weakens uniform language interoperability or still rejects local-only data.

evidence.detail: R4 binding strength is preferred and value set is `ValueSet/languages`.
R6 binding strength is required and value set is `ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4`.
evidence.quote: IETF language tag for a human language

evidence.detail: The R6 all-languages value set includes the BCP-47 system `urn:ietf:bcp:47`.

examples.examplesMd: The old example is valid under a preferred binding but would not satisfy an R6 required BCP-47 language binding. Local operational flags should be moved to another element or extension and replaced here with real language tags.

findings.narrativeMd: `HealthcareService.communication` changed from a recommended language binding to a required all-language binding. This affects directories that used `communication` for local language-support categories, interpreter flags, or text-only/local-coded concepts rather than BCP-47 language tags.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance can become R6-invalid when `communication` contains codings outside `all-languages`. R6-to-R4 representation is not the hard part because R4's preferred binding can carry R6 language codings; the break is R4-to-R6 validation and terminology enforcement. Generated code that narrows code systems or validators that call terminology services need updated tests.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit all `HealthcareService.communication` codings. Convert real languages to BCP-47 codes in `urn:ietf:bcp:47`; move non-language service capabilities to a better element, such as `characteristic`, `eligibility`, a profile extension, or local directory metadata. Test common language codes, regional tags, text-only entries, and legacy local coding systems against the R6 terminology configuration.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stricter binding is aligned with the element's semantics, but a backward-compatible transition could have used extensible strength or required one BCP-47 coding while allowing additional local codings. That would reduce validation failures but permit less consistent data.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A live terminology expansion would improve confidence for edge-case BCP-47 tags and validator behavior for CodeableConcepts containing both valid language codings and extra local codings.

findings.title: Eligibility gained R6-only value and period fields plus a code-required invariant

oldState.summary: R4 eligibility has `code 0..1` and `comment 0..1`; no eligibility value, no period, and no local eligibility invariant.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 eligibility can describe a coded requirement and free-text comment, but cannot carry typed values such as an age range or boolean flag.

newState.summary: R6 eligibility adds `value[x] 0..1`, `period 0..1`, and invariant `hcs-1` requiring `code` when `value[x]` is used.

constraints.human: To use an eligibility value a code must also be provided to determine the type of eligibility the value applies to.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can express eligibility values such as age ranges, boolean new/existing-patient flags, quantities, codeable concepts, or references, and can time-bound the rule.

facts.note: The binding remains example strength, so this part is not a hard validation break.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The new fields are optional, so ordinary R4 instances without them remain structurally migratable. The impact is mainly for R6 producers and converters: R6 `value[x]` and `period` have no native R4 location, and R6 validators enforce `hcs-1` when `value[x]` is present. Generated models add a choice element with several possible types and migration code must preserve or intentionally drop it.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Eligibility values can control whether a person can access a service; losing an age range, referral requirement value, or effective period can change business behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow computable eligibility rules and require the value to be typed by an eligibility code.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the reported `value[x]`, `period`, and invariant are optional R6 additions or constraints on new R6 content.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--making eligibility rules more computable and preventing untyped values--is reasonable. As framed in this finding, the change does not invalidate R4 instances during R4-to-R6 migration because the added fields are optional and `hcs-1` applies when the new value is present. The material issue is R6-to-R4 representability, so the backward-compatible-alternative question for breaking base R6 design is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using R4-compatible extensions or profile conventions could preserve R6 `eligibility.value[x]` and `eligibility.period` when converting down to R4, but that is a cross-version mitigation. Since the base R6 design adds optional expressiveness without removing the R4 `eligibility` shape for old instances, there is no less-breaking base R6 alternative to calibrate for this finding.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions help down-conversion but are migration mitigations, not less-breaking base R6 alternatives.

evidence.detail: R4 eligibility contains only the local child elements `code` and `comment`.
R6 adds `value[x]` with CodeableConcept, boolean, Quantity, Range, and Reference choices.
R6 adds a local invariant requiring `code` when `value[x]` exists.

examples.examplesMd: Plain R4 has no native place for the typed value or eligibility period. A down-converter can summarize in `eligibility.comment`, but that is lossy unless extensions are also used.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes eligibility more computable by adding a typed value and a period. That is useful, but it introduces a choice-type codegen surface and a local invariant. It is not a hard R4-to-R6 instance break for old data, but it is a material R6-to-R4 round-trip risk.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances without `value[x]` are not invalidated by this change. R6 instances that include `eligibility.value[x]` without `eligibility.code` are invalid because of `hcs-1`. Valid R6 eligibility values and periods are not cleanly representable in core R4; they must be reduced to comments, extensions, or profile-specific data.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When upgrading, leave existing `code` and `comment` intact and optionally derive R6 `value[x]` only when the code semantics are known. When down-converting, use extensions for lossless preservation or produce a human-readable `comment` with an explicit loss marker. Tests should cover every allowed value choice type and the missing-code invariant.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The invariant and new fields are reasonable for computable eligibility, but R4 compatibility would have been better served by a standard cross-version extension or by initially publishing this as a profile pattern. The tradeoff is that extensions are less visible to generic clients.

findings.title: `HealthcareService.comment` primitive type changed from string to markdown

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 treats the additional service description as plain string content.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same JSON element name and cardinality but changes the primitive type to markdown, implying formatted text semantics.

facts.note: The wire value remains a JSON string, but generated datatype and rendering semantics can change.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Most plain R4 strings are syntactically usable as markdown and the JSON element remains a string, so this is not usually a hard wire-format break. It is still a codegen and rendering risk: generated models may use a different primitive type, validators may apply markdown-specific rules, and UI renderers may interpret characters such as `*`, `_`, links, or HTML-sensitive content differently.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The field is descriptive, but unsafe or changed rendering could affect directory display or user interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer formatted descriptive comments for display under the service name.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `comment` as `string` and clarify markdown/display expectations, or add a separate optional formatted-comment element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing richer displayed comments is a reasonable goal, but replacing the primitive type from `string` to `markdown` was not clearly necessary to meet it. The JSON shape remains a string, so the main break is generated type and rendering semantics. Retaining the old primitive with clearer definition text, or adding a separate formatted field, would preserve most R4 usage while still allowing R6 implementations to support markdown display. This makes the break probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have left `HealthcareService.comment` as `string` while stating that implementations may interpret it as markdown for display, or could have added an optional `commentMarkdown`-style element and deprecated the plain field over time. The former weakens machine-readable formatting semantics; the latter duplicates display text. Those are moderate tradeoffs compared with changing the existing element's primitive type.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 wire shape and generated APIs, with only moderate tradeoff in type-level formatting standardization or duplicate display fields.

evidence.detail: R4 type code is `string`.
R6 type code is `markdown`.

oldValidNewInvalidJson.comment: Use * only as a literal asterisk in old display code.

examples.examplesMd: The example is not necessarily invalid in R6; it illustrates behaviorally different rendering. A literal asterisk in plain text can become markdown emphasis depending on renderer behavior.

findings.narrativeMd: The `comment` field keeps its name and cardinality but changes primitive type. This is easy to miss because the JSON value is still a string. The break is mostly in generated classes, validators that distinguish primitive types, and display components that now treat the content as markdown instead of plain text.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Most R4 values should remain lexically acceptable in R6, so hard validation failures are only potential. Runtime compatibility is more likely to break: generated APIs may expose a markdown-specific type, sanitization rules may differ, and UI output can change. R6 markdown content can be stored in R4 `string`, but R4 consumers will not necessarily know to render or sanitize it as markdown.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review generated model changes and UI rendering paths. Treat migrated content as untrusted markdown and apply the same sanitization policy used for other FHIR markdown primitives. Regression tests should include plain text, markdown punctuation, links, and content that previously displayed literally.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This could have been fully backward-compatible by retaining `string` and documenting optional markdown conventions or by adding a separate formatted field. The tradeoff would be weaker standardization of formatting semantics.

findings.title: R6 adds `HealthcareService.offeredIn` self-reference with no R4 equivalent

oldState.summary: R4 has no `offeredIn` element for linking a specific schedulable service to a more generic HealthcareService.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can represent service relationships only through other available elements, references outside the resource, or extensions.

semanticText.short: The service within which this service is offered
semanticText.definition: When the HealthcareService is representing a specific, schedulable service, the availableIn property can refer to a generic service.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can explicitly model service hierarchies such as CT Scan offered in a broader Radiology service.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This optional addition does not invalidate R4 instances during upgrade. The risk is loss of service hierarchy on R6-to-R4 conversion and new generated-code/reference traversal behavior in R6 clients.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing generic-to-specific service relationships can affect directory navigation, scheduling grouping, and reporting.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent hierarchical service offerings directly in the resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `offeredIn` is an optional additive R6 element and does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of representing a specific service as offered within a broader HealthcareService is reasonable, and adding an optional self-reference is the normal backward-compatible way to extend the R6 base resource. The risk identified here is loss when converting R6 content back to core R4, not a breaking R4-to-R6 design choice.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: An R4 extension or external relationship table could preserve the hierarchy in R4, but that is a down-conversion strategy. Because R4 instances remain valid without `offeredIn`, the calibration question of a less-breaking base R6 design is not applicable for this finding.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions mitigate down-conversion loss but are not less-breaking alternatives to an optional R6 base addition.

evidence.detail: R6 adds a repeated Reference to HealthcareService.
evidence.quote: The service within which this service is offered

evidence.detail: No R4 local element corresponds to `offeredIn`.

examples.examplesMd: Plain R4 has no native `offeredIn` field; preserving this relationship requires an extension or external relationship store.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a self-reference that lets a specific service point back to a broader service. This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but it matters for round-tripping and for code that builds service catalogs from HealthcareService resources.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to this optional addition. Valid R6 instances using `offeredIn` cannot be represented in core R4 without an extension, so down-conversion can lose service hierarchy. Generated R6 clients must also handle a new self-reference and possible reference cycles in traversal code.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, populate `offeredIn` only when a trustworthy service hierarchy exists. For R6-to-R4, preserve the references through a documented extension or an external mapping table if hierarchy is operationally important. Test graph traversal for cycles and missing referenced services.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A core self-reference is cleaner than an extension for R6 consumers, but an extension would have been more backward-compatible with R4. The tradeoff is between generic visibility in R6 and cross-version representability.

findings.title: R6 adds `HealthcareService.referralRequired` boolean with no native R4 field

oldState.summary: R4 has `referralMethod` but no boolean indicating that a referral is required.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can describe methods of referral, but it lacks a simple access-control flag for whether a referral is mandatory.

semanticText.short: A referral is required for access to this service
semanticText.definition: Indicates whether or not a prospective consumer will require a referral for a particular service at a site to be provided by the Organization.
semanticText.comment: If more than just a general referral is required then you can combine this with the eligibility property.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can state the general referral requirement separately from the permitted referral methods and more detailed eligibility rules.

facts.note: Related in business meaning but not a rename; R4 referralMethod remains present in R6.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The optional boolean does not break existing R4 instances. It is material because R6 data can now carry a direct access requirement that R4 cannot preserve except through comments, eligibility details, extensions, or local business rules.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping a referral-required flag can mislead scheduling, triage, or patient-facing access workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate the fact that a referral is required from the method by which referral can occur.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `referralRequired` is an optional additive R6 element and does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of separating whether a referral is required from the methods of referral is reasonable, and the R6 design adds a simple optional boolean without changing the existing `referralMethod` element. The compatibility issue is that R6 data may not round-trip to plain R4, not that old R4 instances are broken by the base R6 design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A profiled eligibility code or extension can carry the boolean meaning in R4, but that is a mitigation for R6-to-R4 conversion. Since the base R6 addition is optional and preserves R4-to-R6 instance validity, there is no less-breaking base R6 alternative to assess for this finding.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Extensions or eligibility-code conventions are R4 preservation strategies, not less-breaking base R6 alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 adds optional boolean `referralRequired`.
evidence.quote: A referral is required for access to this service

evidence.detail: R4 has referral methods but no corresponding required/not-required boolean.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows a lossy human-readable fallback. A lossless R4 conversion would require an extension.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a direct boolean for whether access requires referral. Although optional, it carries operational meaning that R4 systems do not have a native place to store. Treating it as merely implied by `referralMethod` can be wrong because referral methods and referral requirement are not the same assertion.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 instances are not invalidated by this addition. Valid R6 instances containing `referralRequired` lose computable meaning in plain R4. Runtime code may need to update access-rule logic to check this new boolean in addition to `referralMethod` and eligibility details.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, preserve `referralRequired` in an extension when computability matters; otherwise include it in `eligibility.comment` or local directory metadata with an explicit loss warning. For R4-to-R6, do not infer `referralRequired=true` solely from the existence of `referralMethod` unless local policy confirms that interpretation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding an optional element is the usual backward-compatible forward evolution, but it creates down-conversion risk. A standard extension would have supported R4 and R6 but would not be as easy for generic R6 clients to discover.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The resource keeps the same canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, baseDefinition, and derivation. The status changed from draft to active but does not indicate a rename, removal, split, or merge.

For local elements that remain at the same path, no material min/max cardinality tightening was found. Cardinality effects associated with moved/replaced elements are covered in the contact and availability findings.
Existing R4 reference elements that remain (`providedBy`, `location`, `coverageArea`, and `endpoint`) keep their target profiles. New `offeredIn` is reported separately as an added self-reference.

No local element changed from non-modifier to modifier or vice versa in a material way. R6 explicitly records false defaults for many elements; R4 absence is equivalent to false. `active` remains a modifier.

No material direct `HealthcareService` summary-flag change was found for unchanged same-path local elements. Summary behavior of child elements inside reusable R6 datatypes is delegated to those datatype reports.
No local slicing changes were found in the assigned resource differential.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value additions/removals were found for `HealthcareService`.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex changes were found on direct `HealthcareService` elements. Primitive/datatype-wide limits are out of scope for this resource report.
Serialization-impacting local changes were found and reported for contact and availability. For remaining unchanged same-path elements, no separate serialization change was found.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical resource identity and structural kind are unchanged. Publication status affects maturity/standards interpretation rather than instance validity by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers may treat R6 `HealthcareService` as more stable than R4, but this does not remove the need to handle the local structural breaking changes reported above.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: `specialty` binding weakened from preferred to example
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Weakening a binding from preferred to example does not make previously valid R4 instances invalid in R6; it relaxes terminology expectations while retaining the same c80-practice-codes value set reference.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that used the preferred binding for quality checks may need to decide whether to keep local warnings even though the base R6 binding is weaker.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Example value sets were added for characteristic and eligibility code
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both bindings remain example strength, so the new value set references guide implementers but do not impose hard conformance restrictions on instance codings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The new R6 value sets (`service-mode` and `eligibility`) are useful targets for normalization, but local legacy codes can remain valid at the base-resource level.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: `appointmentRequired` wording was simplified without structural change
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The type, cardinality, and modifier status are unchanged. The revised definition removes duplicated wording but retains the same core meaning.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: No instance transform is needed; documentation or UI labels may be updated to match R6 wording.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `HealthcareService` now depends on `Availability` for schedule-like content. A datatype-level report should own any general `Availability` breaking changes, constraints, summary flags, and cross-artifact reuse issues.
The contact migration depends on how `ExtendedContactDetail` should be represented, validated, and down-converted across FHIR versions.
The snapshots show an inherited language binding change on `HealthcareService.language`. It is excluded from local findings and should be assessed in the base/infrastructure artifact report.
The `communication` breaking-change impact depends on required-binding validation behavior and BCP-47 expansion details.
